A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ST-TTC work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A-G are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, ablations, sensitivity studies, and efficiency measurements, including Tables 2-4 and appendix Tables 6-8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendix Tables E.1-E.3, with additional significance annotations in Table 3.

M1.justification: The spectral calibrator, grouped amplitude/phase modulation, frozen backbone, FIFO queue, and single-step updates are unchanged. The new main-text zero-initialization note describes behavior already present in v1's Appendix C.1 pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 14 datasets and retain standard, few-shot, 24-step, large-scale, OOD, and continual-learning scenarios. The longer forecasting horizons discussed in new Appendix F.1 are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments. Table 3 retains TTT-MAE, TENT, CompFormer, OnlineTCN, FSNet, OneNet, and DOST; the backbone and specialized-learning comparisons are also preserved.

E3.justification: The splits, forecasting windows, metrics, 10% few-shot training subset, OOD settings, and training budgets remain unchanged. Sections 5.1 and D.3 retain the same calibration learning rate, group count, and update settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 retains the same calibration, node-sharing, sample-selection, and parameter-sensitivity analyses. OOD analyses and prediction cases are preserved, including v1 Figure 9 as v2 Figure F.1; the new horizon discussion supplies no additional empirical analysis.

E5.justification: v2 introduces t-test significance annotations with p < 0.01 in Table 3. Both versions already specify five repetitions and mean ± standard deviation; additional runs are not established, and the new caption does not identify the reference comparison.

E6.justification: Matched forecasting scores, standard deviations, and efficiency results are unchanged. Table 3 newly marks ST-TTC's regular-setting MAE of 3.46 ± 0.01 and online-setting MAE/RMSE of 3.77 ± 0.07 and 7.75 ± 0.13 as significant, adding statistical findings rather than performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Theorem 1 now characterize the perturbation bound as approximate, while Remark 1 changes 'linearly' to 'sub-linearly' bounded. The displayed inequalities, first-order derivation, assumptions, and Proposition 2 remain unchanged; no revised proof supports the new sublinear characterization.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about calibration-based test-time computing, its two components, and its effectiveness, universality, flexibility, and efficiency.

C2.justification: New Appendix F.1 explains the practical and computational rationale for 12/24-step forecasting, connects a cited spectral-complexity law to single-step calibration, and questions conclusions about traffic-model saturation. The earlier limitations and future-work directions remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an ST-TTC repository link and a 'Fully Open Source' statement on its first page; v1 provided pseudocode and baseline links without this project-access information. The implementation listings, hardware, and detailed hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds positioning around forecasting horizons and predictability through Bergmeir (2024), Brigato et al. (2025), Zheng et al. (2025), and Wang et al. (2025b). The central positioning against existing forecasting and test-time learning methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. v2 adds acknowledgments and Appendix F.1, shortens the repetitive limitations preamble, adds localized explanations, and changes numbered citations to author-year citations.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns presentation throughout: a shaded title/abstract panel, changed typography and text width, restyled captions and code listings, and appendix navigation links. Figure 3 replaces connected curves and shaded bands with separate points and error bars; tables and the retained prediction-case figure are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added code-access information, forecasting-horizon rationale in Appendix F.1, and clearer categorical display in Figure 3 modestly improve accessibility and interpretation. These benefits are limited by Table 3's unspecified significance comparator and Appendix B.1's unsupported new 'sub-linearly' wording. The underlying method and empirical conclusions remain stable.
